The pattern suggests a period when the Fed has cut sharply (policy rate down 1.5 z over 3 months and 12 months), the dollar has surged (+2.5 over 3 months), the 10-year yield has risen, and unemployment is elevated relative to its 3-year average (+2.0). The most likely fit is late 2024 to early 2025.

Against that fit, the unemployment rate is high versus its 3-year average, and the 12-month change is +1.0 (it rose from about 3.7% to about 4.1–4.2%). The Fed cut 100bp from September to December 2024. The 10-year yield rose from about 3.6% to 4.6% over the autumn. The dollar jumped in Q4 2024. Core CPI is low against its own history, which also fits, and the stock-bond correlation had turned negative at that point.

December 2024 is the best candidate: Treasuries fell 1.0 over 1 month (December 2024 was weak), equities fell about 2.5% that month, and gold fell slightly. January 2025 is the alternative. In that month equities rose and Treasuries were flat, so December fits better. The 3-month dollar change of +2.5 also fits December, since the dollar rose strongly from October to December.
